bread-whole-wheat-with-raisins-toasted.title: Whole Wheat Bread with Raisins, Toasted

content.title: About
content.content: Whole wheat bread with raisins is a loaf made from whole grain wheat flour, enriched with dried grapes and toasted to a golden crust. It combines the nutty flavor of toasted bread, the natural sweetness of raisins, and the nutrition of whole grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole wheat bread contains all parts of the grain—bran, germ, and endosperm—making it more nutritious than white bread.
Raisins retain many of their antioxidants, such as polyphenols, even after baking.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crunchy crust while preserving most nutrients.
This type of bread is traditional in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines.
The combination of whole grains and dried fruit provides a steady source of energy for athletes.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains deliver a substantial amount of fiber, supporting healthy digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The loaf provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Natural antioxidants
items.content: Raisins add polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Whole wheat bread has a lower GI than white bread, contributing to more stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins contribute natural sugars, so individuals monitoring glucose should consider portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The product contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasted bread is more calorie‑dense; moderate portions are important for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread as a snack, spread with butter or avocado, use in sandwiches, serve alongside soups, or make croutons. Toasted slices pair well with cheese and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, place it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 3 months.

chicken-or-turkey-with-mushroom-sauce.title: Chicken or Turkey with Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey prepared with a delicate mushroom sauce is a balanced dish rich in protein and aromatic mushrooms. The meat is tender and juicy, while the sauce adds an earthy flavor and creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms contain vitamin D, which is produced when they are exposed to ultraviolet light.
Turkey is high in tryptophan, an amino acid that supports serotonin production.
Chicken is one of the most affordable sources of high‑quality protein worldwide.
Mushroom sauce is often made with cream, broth, and fresh herbs, making it versatile for many meals.
Traditionally, this dish is served with mashed potatoes or rice.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat (especially skinless chicken breast)
items.content: Skin‑less meat contains little saturated fat, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the meat and mushrooms supply B6, niacin, and riboflavin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Mushrooms add potassium, selenium, and copper, while turkey contributes zinc and iron.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Selenium from mushrooms and zinc from meat help maintain a healthy immune system.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter.

items.title: High sodium in sauce
items.content: If the sauce is prepared with a lot of salt, it may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Prepared sauces may contain artificial preservatives and flavor enhancers.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and a drizzle of extra sauce. It pairs well with boiled potatoes, rice, couscous, or a fresh vegetable salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then place in an airtight container and refrigerate for no more than 2‑3 days. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.

egg-white-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Egg White, Cooked, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear liquid surrounding the yolk. When boiled without added fat it becomes a firm, tender piece that is rich in protein and virtually free of fat and carbohydrates. It is widely used in diet plans, muscle‑building diets, and various culinary applications.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white is about 90 % water and the rest is high‑quality protein.
100 g of boiled egg white provides over 10 g of protein and less than 0.2 g of fat.
It contains no cholesterol, unlike the yolk.
Heat denatures the proteins, changing their structure while preserving all essential amino acids.
Egg white is a key ingredient in meringues, soufflés, and fat‑free omelets.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Provides all essential amino acids, making it ideal for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Approximately 52 kcal per 100 g of boiled egg white, supporting weight‑management goals.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Suitable for low‑salt dietary regimes.

items.title: No fat or cholesterol
items.content: Helps maintain cardiovascular health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Biotin availability
items.content: Raw egg whites contain avidin, which binds biotin; cooking destroys avidin, but large amounts of cooked whites can still affect biotin status.

items.title: Lack of other nutrients
items.content: Egg white is low in iron, calcium, and vitamin D, so it should not be the sole source of nutrition.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled egg white can be eaten as a snack, diced into salads, added to soups, used in fat‑free omelets, or blended into protein shakes. It stores well sliced in the fridge for up to 3 days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep boiled egg white in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C for no more than 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Long rice noodles are thin, translucent noodles made from mung bean starch (green pea). When cooked they become firm yet slightly chewy with a neutral flavor, making them versatile for a wide range of Asian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: These noodles are a staple in Thai, Vietnamese, and Chinese cuisines.
They are completely gluten‑free, suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
Mung bean starch gives the noodles a high degree of transparency after cooking, adding visual appeal to dishes.
Often served cold in salads or hot in soups and stir‑fries.
Mung beans, also called green peas, are a good source of plant protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The noodles contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides sustained energy and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Safe for those who must avoid gluten.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Mung bean starch contributes a modest amount of protein, beneficial for vegetarians.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Can help moderate blood sugar levels when consumed in reasonable portions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to legumes, including mung beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in excess.

items.title: Digestive comfort
items.content: Large servings may cause gas or bloating in people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil the noodles for 3–5 minutes, then rinse with cold water. Use them in soups, stir‑fries, salads, or spring rolls. Pair with sauces, vegetables, seafood, or tofu for a complete meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry noodles in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked noodles should be stored in the refrigerator and consumed within 1–2 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Nutella sandwich on white bread is a simple snack made of two slices of white bread spread with sweet Nutella paste, which contains hazelnuts, cocoa and vegetable oils.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nutella was created in Italy in 1964 and quickly became popular worldwide.
The combination of sweet spread and soft white bread makes the sandwich a favorite for both children and adults.
One sandwich typically provides about 200–250 kcal, depending on the thickness of the spread.
Nutella contains about 13 % hazelnuts, but most of the flavor comes from sugar and vegetable oils.
The sandwich can be prepared at home in just a few seconds.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and fats in Nutella deliver quick energy, making it a convenient fast snack.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Hazelnuts provide a modest amount of iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Nutella supplies small amounts of B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from bread
items.content: White bread is often fortified with calcium, which contributes to bone health.

items.title: Pleasurable taste
items.content: The sweet flavor can improve mood by triggering endorphin release.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Regular consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: The vegetable oils in Nutella contain saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: The spread contains hazelnuts, which can cause allergic reactions.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: White bread contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single sandwich can contain up to 250 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread Nutella evenly on one slice of white bread, place the second slice on top, and optionally cut into halves. You can add banana, strawberries or extra nuts for variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Nutella refrigerated after opening in a tightly sealed jar, and store bread in a dry place or a bag. For longer storage, freeze the bread to prevent it from drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Ranch dressing is a popular American sauce made from mayonnaise, sour cream and buttermilk, flavored with garlic, onion, dill, parsley and spices. It has a creamy texture and a distinctive herbaceous taste, commonly used as a salad dressing, dip for vegetables, wings and french fries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ranch was first created in the 1950s in the United States at the Hidden Valley Ranch restaurant.
It has been the best‑selling dressing in the U.S. for more than 30 years.
The original recipe used buttermilk, but mass‑produced versions often replace it with cream or yogurt.
Ranch is frequently used in culinary experiments: on pizza, in marinades, and even in desserts.
In Russia Ranch dressing became popular in the early 2000s, appearing in chain restaurants and supermarkets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Sour cream and buttermilk provide calcium, which is important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mayonnaise and dairy components supply modest amounts of vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: When fermented buttermilk is used, the dressing can contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The sauce contains milk, cream and eggs, which may trigger reactions in people with relevant allergies.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Ranch dressing is calorie‑dense and rich in saturated fats, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared versions often contain added salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ranch dressing is used as a salad dressing, dip for vegetables, wings, fries, and as a sauce for burgers and sandwiches. It can be added to marinades or blended with other sauces for new flavor profiles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Ranch dressing in the refrigerator at 1 °C–4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 1–2 weeks. Discard the dressing if it develops an off‑odor, color change, or mold.
